NEXUS CORP INTERNAL WORKPLACE & HUMAN RESOURCES POLICIES

1. Flexible Working Hours and Core Schedules
Nexus Corp operates on a flexible scheduling policy designed to accommodate diverse working preferences while maintaining strong team collaboration. Core collaboration hours across all time zones are established from 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM EST. During these core hours, all full-time employees are expected to be available on Slack and respond to critical team inquiries within a 30-minute window. Ou

tical team inquiries within a 30-minute window. Outside of core hours, employees are free to structure their working days as they see fit, provided they complete 40 hours per week and attend mandatory synchronous group meetings.

2. Annual Paid Time Off (PTO) and Leave Policies
All full-time employees are granted 22 days of paid time off per calendar year. PTO accrues on a pro-rata basis at the rate of 1.83 days for every fully worked calendar month. Employees must submit PTO requests through th

nth. Employees must submit PTO requests through the HR portal at least 7 days in advance for short absences (1-2 days) and 21 days in advance for extended leave (3 or more consecutive business days). A maximum of 5 unused PTO days can be carried over into the following calendar year, and these carried-over days expire on March 31st if unused.

3. Parental and Caregiver Leave
Nexus Corp provides 14 weeks of fully paid parental leave for primary caregivers following the birth, adoption, or foster

regivers following the birth, adoption, or foster placement of a child. Secondary caregivers are eligible for 6 weeks of fully paid leave. Employees must give HR at least 30 days written notice before starting parental leave. Leave must be taken within the first 12 months of the child's arrival.

4. Wellness Allowance and Home Office Setup
To support remote employees, Nexus Corp offers a $100 monthly stipend usable for high-speed home internet, mobile phone plans, or co-working space day passes.

obile phone plans, or co-working space day passes. Additionally, newly hired full-time employees receive a one-time $750 ergonomic allowance to purchase desks, office chairs, external monitors, or peripheral equipment. Receipts must be submitted to the HR portal within 60 days of hire.

5. Code of Conduct and Anti-Harassment Policy
Nexus Corp is committed to providing a safe, respectful, and inclusive environment for everyone. Discriminatory behavior, harassment, or intimidation based on race, g

vior, harassment, or intimidation based on race, gender, sexual orientation, disability, or religion is strictly prohibited. Violations should be reported immediately to hr-ethics@nexuscorp.com. Reports are investigated within 5 business days, and non-compliance may lead to immediate termination.

NEXUS CORP CUSTOMER SUPPORT & SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENTS (SLA)

1. Ticket Severity Levels and Target Response Times
Customer support requests submitted to Nexus Corp are categorized into three distinct severity levels: Critical (P1), Major (P2), and Minor (P3). P1 issues involve total system outages or severe data corruption affecting production environments; these require an initial response from the engineering team within 15 minutes and status updates every 30 minutes. P2 issues involve degrade

pdates every 30 minutes. P2 issues involve degraded performance or broken core functionality without complete system downtime, carrying a 2-hour response SLA. P3 issues cover general inquiries, how-to questions, and non-blocking feature requests, carrying a 24-hour response window.

2. Support Channels, Coverage, and Operating Hours
Standard customer support is available via email at support@nexuscorp.com and through our web portal from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM EST, Monday through Friday. Dedicated 24

o 8:00 PM EST, Monday through Friday. Dedicated 24/7 emergency phone support and private Slack Connect channels are strictly reserved for Enterprise tier customers who encounter P1 critical incidents outside of standard business hours.

3. Automated Ticket Routing and Escalation Procedures
Incoming tickets are automatically categorized and assigned using AI-based text routing. If a P1 or P2 support ticket exceeds its response SLA window without active progress logged by an engineer, it automatic

ctive progress logged by an engineer, it automatically escalates to the Duty Support Manager. If the issue remains unresolved after 4 hours, the escalation transfers directly to the VP of Customer Success and the Lead Infrastructure Engineer on call.

4. Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) and Quality Assurance
Following the closure of every support ticket, an automated customer satisfaction survey is dispatched to the submitter requesting a rating from 1 to 5 stars alongside optional qualitative feedb

1 to 5 stars alongside optional qualitative feedback. Any survey returned with a rating of 2 stars or below triggers an automatic review by the Support Quality Assurance Lead within 48 hours to determine root causes and improve agent training.

5. Service Credits for SLA Breaches
For Enterprise tier customers, Nexus Corp guarantees a monthly system uptime availability of 99.9%. If system availability drops below 99.9% in any calendar month, affected customers are eligible to claim service credi

cted customers are eligible to claim service credits equal to 10% of their monthly subscription fee. Requests for service credits must be submitted to billing@nexuscorp.com within 30 days of the affected month's end.

NEXUS CORP INFORMATION SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE GUIDELINES

1. Password Security and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
All corporate email accounts, code repositories, internal databases, and administrative tools strictly require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Authentication requests must be verified via the Okta Authenticator application or hardware YubiKeys. Standard passwords must be a minimum of 16 characters long and must contain a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, num

ation of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols. Corporate passwords must be updated every 90 days, and the system automatically prevents reusing any of the previous 8 passwords.

2. Device Encryption, Endpoint Protection, and Software Controls
All company-issued laptops must run full file system encryption (FileVault on macOS or BitLocker on Windows platforms). Employees are strictly forbidden from disabling CrowdStrike endpoint protection software, modifying local f

ke endpoint protection software, modifying local firewall settings, or installing unapproved third-party software applications. Personal USB drives and unapproved external storage hardware are automatically blocked by device management software to prevent corporate data leakage.

3. Phishing Protocols and Security Incident Reporting
If an employee suspects they have received a phishing email or inadvertently clicked an unsafe external link, they must isolate their computer from Wi-Fi immediately

must isolate their computer from Wi-Fi immediately. The incident must be reported to the Security Operations Center (SOC) via email to security-alert@nexuscorp.com or through the emergency #sec-incidents Slack channel within 15 minutes.

4. Remote Access and Virtual Private Network (VPN)
Accessing internal staging environments, internal wiki pages, or production servers requires an active encrypted connection through the corporate VPN. Connecting to corporate resources via unsecured public Wi-Fi

to corporate resources via unsecured public Wi-Fi networks without an active VPN is a direct violation of IT policy. VPN sessions automatically log out after 12 hours of inactivity, requiring re-authentication via MFA.

5. Data Classification and Offboarding Controls
Data at Nexus Corp is classified into three tiers: Public, Internal, and Restricted. Restricted data includes customer personally identifiable information (PII) and financial records, which must never be stored on local drives. Whe

s, which must never be stored on local drives. When an employee departs the company, IT automatically revokes access to all systems at 5:00 PM on their final day, and physical hardware must be returned via pre-paid shipping within 7 days.

NEXUS PLATFORM TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE AND INFRASTRUCTURE

1. Microservices Infrastructure and API Protocols
The Nexus core platform is built as a set of decoupled microservices hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) using Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS). Primary services communicate synchronously using RESTful JSON APIs over HTTPS protocols, while asynchronous event-driven workflows rely on Apache Kafka topic pipelines for heavy background processing jobs, notification dispatching, and analytics d

ng jobs, notification dispatching, and analytics data ingestion.

2. Database Engines and Caching Layer Strategy
Primary structured operational data is stored in PostgreSQL database clusters deployed using AWS Aurora with multi-region read replicas for fault tolerance. For high-throughput key-value operations, session storage, and rate-limiting, the architecture uses Redis clusters. All data at rest is encrypted using AES-256 keys managed by AWS Key Management Service (KMS), and data in transit

Key Management Service (KMS), and data in transit is enforced using TLS 1.3.

3. Continuous Integration and Deployment (CI/CD) Pipelines
Code updates pushed to GitHub repositories trigger automated verification pipelines using GitHub Actions. Every Pull Request requires passing automated unit testing, integration tests, static code analysis via SonarQube, and approval from at least two senior peer code reviewers before merging into the main branch. Automated deployments to production take place

h. Automated deployments to production take place daily during low-traffic windows at 02:00 UTC.

4. System Monitoring, Logging, and Observability
System metrics, cluster health, and error logs are collected across all nodes using Prometheus and visualized via Grafana dashboards. Centralized application logging is handled by Datadog. Synthetic monitoring alerts trigger automated PagerDuty notifications to the designated infrastructure engineer on call if API response latencies exceed 500ms or if

call if API response latencies exceed 500ms or if error rates surpass 1% over a 5-minute rolling window.

5. Disaster Recovery and Data Backup Protocols
Database snapshots are automatically captured every 1 hour and stored across geographically isolated AWS availability zones. Full system backups are performed weekly and retained for 90 days. The platform target Recovery Point Objective (RPO) is under 15 minutes, and the target Recovery Time Objective (RTO) is under 2 hours in the event of a ca
ective (RTO) is under 2 hours in the event of a catastrophic regional cloud failure.

NEXUS CORP TRAVEL AND EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY

1. Booking Flights, Rail, and Hotel Accommodations
All domestic and international business travel must be arranged at least 14 days prior to departure through the corporate travel management portal (Navan). For domestic flights under 6 hours, standard economy class is required. Business class booking is permitted for continuous international flights exceeding 8 total hours. Hotel accommodations must not exceed $250 per night in standard metropo

must not exceed $250 per night in standard metropolitan areas or $350 per night in designated high-cost cities like New York, London, and Tokyo.

2. Daily Food Allowances (Per Diem) and Client Meals
Employees traveling on official company business receive a flat daily meal allowance (per diem) of $80 per day. Itemized receipts are mandatory for any individual food or beverage expense that exceeds $25. Alcoholic beverages are not eligible for reimbursement under standard meal allowances unless pa

bursement under standard meal allowances unless part of an authorized client entertainment event pre-approved in writing by a Vice President.

3. Ground Transportation and Mileage Reimbursement
Travelers are encouraged to use public transit or rideshare services (Uber/Lyft) when traveling to and from airports and client locations. Premium or luxury car rides are strictly prohibited. Personal vehicle usage for business trips is reimbursed at the standard IRS mileage rate, provided the employee su

tandard IRS mileage rate, provided the employee submits start and end addresses along with toll receipts.

4. Expense Reimbursement Submissions and Approval Workflows
Expense reports must be filed within 30 calendar days of completing a trip using the Expensify platform. Digital copies or clean JPEG photo scans of itemized receipts must be attached to every claimed item. Expense reports submitted after 45 days will be automatically rejected by the finance department and will not be eligible for

e finance department and will not be eligible for reimbursement. Approved expenses are paid out via direct deposit every second Friday.

5. Corporate Credit Card Usage Rules
Executive team members and frequent travelers who hold corporate credit cards must submit monthly reconciliation statements by the 5th of each month. Personal expenses made on corporate credit cards, even if accidental, must be reported to finance immediately and reimbursed within 10 business days.
